correctness.rationale: For any convex body L of dimension d, the normalized reflection-volume polynomial has coefficients binom(d,j) V_d(L[d-j],-L[j])/vol(L). Alexandrov--Fenchel log-concavity and the equal endpoint volumes give the coefficientwise lower envelope (1+t)^d, and the proved Godbersen inequality gives the upper envelope F_d(t)=sum_j binom(d,j)^2 t^j. Cartesian products multiply these polynomials. The Vandermonde square inequality F_a F_b <=_coeff F_{a+b} merges all but one factor. The proven coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of type-B Narayana polynomials yields F_{a-1}F_{n-a+1}>=_coeff F_aF_{n-a} for 2<=a<=n/2, so F_1F_{n-1} is the sharp upper envelope. Extracting its k-th coefficient and normalizing produces [k^2+(n-k)^2]/n^2. Equality throughout the upper envelope forces the maximal partition of the first coefficient, hence dimensions 1 and n-1, and equality in the factor Godbersen theorem forces a simplex; the converse is direct. The lower envelope equality is equivalent to Brunn--Minkowski difference-body equality and central symmetry. The actual included checker passed 1048469 exact coefficient comparisons for all ordered factor partitions through dimension sixteen; independent exact shoelace geometry checked an asymmetric trapezoid factor.

value.rationale: The sharp, all-index improvement 1-2k(n-k)/n^2 quantifies rigidity of the recently solved Godbersen inequality on the structurally natural and broad class of all affinely product-decomposable full-dimensional convex bodies. Central indices force approximately a fifty-percent reduction from the universal simplex coefficient, uniformly in dimension; the exact upper equality shape is a prism over a simplex, whereas the lower edge is governed by central symmetry. This quantifies a meaningful geometric separation rather than a single special-value computation or a routine restatement. The structural bridge from general convex mixed volumes to nontrivial Narayana Hankel-total positivity supplies the needed proof.
